original_idea.title: Post-Deployment Capability Elicitation + Evaluation Obsolescence
original_idea.problem: Model capabilities can be elicited after deployment through in-context learning, fine-tuning, or jailbreaks in ways not anticipated at evaluation time. Evaluation obsolescence compounds with capability elicitation.
original_idea.direction: Test post-deployment elicitation scenarios: take a model that passes safety benchmarks, apply progressively sophisticated elicitation techniques, and measure at what elicitation complexity safety breaks down. Compare elicitation vulnerability across models with different safety training intensities.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Post-deployment elicitation is the adversarial version of evaluation-deployment gaps. A model that is safe at eval time but unsafe after simple elicitation is a deployment risk.
original_idea.relevant_context: Hubinger et al. 'sleeper agents' research shows capabilities can be dormant in evaluation. Fine-tuning API misuse is a documented deployment threat.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: measuring elicitation thresholds directly informs deployment risk assessment and motivates continuous post-deployment monitoring. Each link is explicit.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Applying progressively sophisticated jailbreaks and elicitation techniques is intermediate. However, lightweight fine-tuning requires some ML experience beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Progressive elicitation across multiple techniques and models requires sustained effort. Could be scoped to jailbreaks only (no fine-tuning) on 2 models for 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: Post-deployment elicitation is well-studied. 'Eliciting Harmful Capabilities by Fine-Tuning on Safeguarded Outputs' (arxiv 2601.13528) directly demonstrates frontier models used to elicit dangerous capabilities from open-source models. Fine-tuning jailbreaks under constrained settings (arxiv 2510.01342) show practical attacks. 'Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep' (OpenReview) shows shallow alignment is easily bypassed. The specific progressive elicitation complexity ladder and comparison across safety training intensities adds some methodology, but the core finding -- that deployed models are vulnerable to post-deployment elicitation -- is well-established.
